title: Release train schedule slices, RC tagging, and notes automation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We currently perform weekly release cuts and RC promotions using semi-manual scripting and ad-hoc PRs. This causes variability in RC timing, inconsistent tagging, and manual assembly of release notes that slows down rollouts and complicates LTS channel management. Goal: Define a deterministic weekly release slice (time-boxed cut window), implement an automated RC tagging pipeline, and auto-generate candidate release notes from curated changelog sources. This ticket covers the scheduling slices, tagging rules, release-notes assembly, and integration points with upgrade tooling and LTS channels. Out of scope: on-prem installer packaging and post-release migration tooling (handled in separate EPIC).
acceptance_criteria: Weekday-based release slice defined and documented (UTC cut window + freeze time)
Automated CI job creates an RC branch and applies semantic RC tag following agreed naming (eg. v1.22.0-rc.2026-03-XX)
Release notes draft auto-assembled from merged PRs labeled 'release-note' and from the changelog generator in the repo
Upgrade-tool compatibility checks run as part of the RC pipeline (smoke migrations + schema checks)
LTS channel mapping updated: weekly RCs can be promoted to minor LTS trains only after gated checks pass
Console and release dashboard updated with RC metadata (tag, cut time, blocker list)
implementation_steps: Design: finalize cut-window policy (proposed: Thursdays 02:00-05:00 UTC freeze, cut at 03:00 UTC)
Create CI pipeline that: 1) creates rc branch from stable/main, 2) runs unit/integration smoke tests, 3) tags RC with timestamped rc metadata
Implement release-note assembler that collects PR titles, 'release-note' labels, and changelog entries into a Markdown draft stored as a release artifact
Add an "upgrade-check" stage that runs the upgrade tooling against a canary cluster and collects migration/pass metrics
Hook pipeline results to release dashboard with a standardized JSON artifact for downstream tooling
Document flow in the release runbook and add a short checklist for on-call and release engineers
rollout_plan: Pilot: run automated cut on a non-LTS minor (runtime-1.22-alpha) for two weekly cycles
Validate RC promotion rules and release-note quality with engineering and PM reviewers
Enable automatic RC tagging for the main weekly train after sign-off
Gradually enable upgrade checks gating for LTS candidates; initial promotion remains manual until two successful gated promotions
Measure metrics (cut success rate, time-to-draft-notes) and iterate
testing_plan: Unit tests for tag and branch creation logic
End-to-end pipeline test using a synthetic repo snapshot
Canary upgrade run in staging with synthetic traffic and schema migration assertions
User acceptance: PM/Eng review of auto-generated release note drafts for two pilot cuts
Chaos test: simulate partial CI failures and verify graceful rollback of RC tagging step
monitoring: Cut success/failed rate metric emitted to internal dashboard
RC pipeline latency histogram (queue -> tag completion)
Alerts for failed upgrade-check stage or missing release-note artifacts
Audit log entries for created tags/branches shipped to S3 for retention
